question: What year-over-year change in US Cyber Monday online spending will Adobe report for 2026?

calls.reasoning: Adobe's Sept 2026 forecast: CM $15.1B (+6.2% per Adobe; +5.96% vs the $14.25B resolution base). Over 2022-2025 actual CM growth beat Adobe's pre-season forecast every year (+0.7, +4.2, +1.2, +0.8pp); 2021 missed by about 5pp. Median set at forecast +~1pp, about +7.0% (~$15.25B). Spending moving to Black Friday and earlier in Cyber Week (Adobe projects BF +9.2%) limits the upside. No prediction market found (Kalshi, Polymarket, Manifold). Escape outside -5/+15 judged negligible.
calls.dossier:
- Adobe 2026 holiday forecast (news.adobe.com, Sept 28 2026): Cyber Monday Nov 30 $15.1B, +6.2% YoY per Adobe (vs the question's $14.25B base, $15.1B = +5.96%, so Adobe likely uses a revised 2025 base). Black Friday $12.9B +9.2%; Thanksgiving $6.9B; Cyber Week $47.5B +7.4%; full Nov-Dec season $275.1B +6.7%; November $145.1B. Discounts similar to 2025 (up to 30%). BNPL on CM $1.09B. AI traffic +130%.
- Adobe forecast vs actual CM history (from memory of Adobe releases, unverified this run): 2025 forecast $14.2B (+6.3%), actual $14.25B (+7.1%); 2024 forecast $13.2B (+6.1%), actual $13.3B (+7.3%); 2023 forecast $11.6B (+5.4%), actual $12.4B (+9.6%); 2022 forecast $11.2B (+5.1%), actual $11.3B (+5.8%); 2021 forecast ~$11.3B, actual $10.7B (-1.4%); 2020 large miss during the pandemic.
- Structural: Black Friday growth beating Cyber Monday growth (2025 BF +9.1% vs CM +7.1%) as spending moves earlier in Cyber Week.
- Resolution: resolves off Adobe's first full-day dollar figure divided by $14.25B (4 sig figs), not Adobe's own stated %, unless Adobe gives only a %. If Adobe rounds to $0.1B: $15.0B=5.26%, $15.1B=5.96%, $15.2B=6.67%, $15.3B=7.37%, $15.4B=8.07%. In 2025 Adobe reported two decimals ($14.25B).
- Event window: Cyber Monday Nov 30 2026 (single day); as of Nov 9 2026 the event hasn't started (0% elapsed). Adobe usually reports Dec 1.
- Markets: none found on Kalshi, Polymarket or Manifold.
- Searched but not found: Adobe data on November 2026 spending so far, a post-September forecast revision, macro/tariff/price-inflation commentary in Adobe's release.

calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the facts: Adobe forecast $15.1B (+6.2%), resolution base $14.25B, $0.1B rounding steps of about 0.7pt, and recent beats of forecast. Their medians (6.7-7.0) differ only on judgment. I re-expressed the historical beats in dollars ($0.05-0.4B, typical $0.1B) and mapped them onto the resolution base, which gives a median near 6.7-6.9 and a mild right skew from the 2023-type beat. I chose 6.8. The forecast history is recalled from memory and could not be verified (no web access), so I kept the tails as wide as the widest run. No escape mass outside -5/+15 is declared.
